PROBE Companies House REST API keyless GET: HTTP 401, body starts "{\"error\":\"Empty Authorization header\",\"type\":\"ch:service\"}" (observed 2026-10-07, single GET, no retry) — a real public REST API that answers unauthenticated requests with a structured auth challenge: free registered API keys, an auth model, not a bot wall.

PROBE GOV.UK Content API keyless GET: HTTP 200 at https://www.gov.uk/api/content/set-up-business, JSON body present (observed 2026-10-07) — the one-stop layer above the registry serves every guidance page as keyless JSON, a machine rail with no US analogue.
PROBE llms.txt: HTTP 404 at https://www.gov.uk/llms.txt (observed 2026-10-07) — even GOV.UK, the best-instrumented government platform in this arena, publishes no agent-oriented docs index.

The register is machine-readable by design: "Companies House digitally records almost all information it receives, and makes this available to the public through its own website and through the Companies House RESTful API." The developer suite publishes dedicated Authorisation, Rate limiting and API versioning guides alongside it.

Versioning posture is published and candid: the API is at beta, "We have a proposed approach to versioning the API and documentation", with existing resources explicitly held 'as is' as version 0 while the approach is discussed in the public Developer Hub Forum.

An identity-verification wall is rolling across the register's write paths: the agency's own news page carries guidance on "when you need to verify your identity for Companies House", including identity verification details for people with significant control (PSC).
Non-UK founders are inside the service's own scope statement: "We hold the UK’s register of companies and the Register of Overseas Entities."
